svg.text: Rover comms & power: no network switch, 24 V electronics bus from the 48 V battery string
Pi 5 is the router: Starlink = WAN 1 on onboard eth0, nearby Wi-Fi = WAN 2 (failover), camera on USB Ethernet eth1. Pi cuts Starlink power when local Wi-Fi is good.
TELEM2 ↔ Pi UART (GPIO14/15): MAVLink, no USB power backfeed
12 V tap between ㉓ and ㉔
mixed mode → ⑭ L + R tracks
two leads: upper 24 V, lower 12 V
1) Hardware: ③ rover E-stop, ㉓ wireless E-stop and ㉔ deadman in series on the
12 V + 24 V leads. ⑫ drops (tracks stop), ⑯ stops the engine and the blade.
2) ArduPilot: ch5 released → Hold; ③ / ㉓ open → ⑮ unpowered → RC failsafe → Hold.
E-stop / disarm leave steering live: ch2 alone spins the tracks.
Electronics run from the 24 V tap; loads on a tap unbalance the string, ⑥ evens it.
While ⑲ charges, the 24 V tap rises to ~29 V (14.4 V per battery): inside the
5 V buck's 32 V and the Starlink relay's 30 V limits. Keep Starlink on the 24 V
tap: the full string runs above the Mini's 48 V maximum while charging.
About 3× longer runtime while Wi-Fi is in range.
No network switch: saves ~1–3 W and a box.
Starlink needs ~1–3 min to reconnect after power-on.
